horizon_driver: Fund vintage/investment-period structure (typically 5-10yr closed-end) plus LP fundraising cycles (~3-5yr) and GP carry-realisation timelines set the true horizon; but growing use of evergreen/interval retail vehicles with periodic redemption windows is compressing the effective horizon toward the liquidity terms offered to end-investors, which the underlying assets cannot actually support.

constraints.source: IMF Global Financial Stability Report (Oct 2025) explicitly warned that valuation uncertainty 'could incentivize fund managers to delay the realization of losses,' and that insurers holding complex, leveraged private-credit instruments could face larger-than-expected losses in a stress scenario
constraints.breaks_under: forced external re-marking via a redemption gate, a bankruptcy/restructuring event, or third-party rating-agency scrutiny — Fitch reported the US private-credit default rate hit a record 6.0% in April 2026, which mechanically forces marks that internal discretion had been delaying

constraints.source: NAIC's Capital Markets Bureau found systemic inflation in private letter ratings on a 2023 sample of 109 privately-rated credit instruments held by insurers, allowing favourable regulatory capital treatment despite underlying risk (NAIC Insurance Topics: Private Credit; BigGo Finance, 2025-26 coverage)
constraints.breaks_under: NAIC's Statutory Accounting Principles Working Group has already adopted revised annual-filing requirements effective year-end 2026 to force better disclosure — the constraint is actively being priced out by regulators in real time

stated_vs_revealed.stated: Private credit is marketed as a lower-volatility, 'patient capital' alternative to public leveraged loans/high-yield — its infrequent marking is presented as a reflection of genuinely illiquid, hold-to-maturity assets rather than a source of hidden risk, and default/loss rates are framed as structurally lower than syndicated markets due to tighter covenants and direct lender-borrower relationships.
stated_vs_revealed.revealed: The US private-credit default rate hit a record 6.0% in April 2026 (Fitch Ratings, May 2026); a ~$265bn market dislocation was underway by March 2026 described in the financial press as a 'meltdown' hitting Blackstone, KKR, Apollo, Ares and Blue Owl; the BIS's March 2026 Quarterly Review flagged AI-driven disruption concentrating losses in software-heavy portfolios alongside intensifying investor redemptions at retail-facing funds; the IMF separately confirmed the mark-discretion problem is a live, named policy concern, not a hypothetical one.
stated_vs_revealed.delta: Large and now realised, not merely theoretical. The Cartographer's framing of NBFI_CREDIT as 'fastest-growing, least-observed' credit was correct in 2024-25 and by 2026 the invisibility itself became the story once losses had to surface.

stated_vs_revealed.stated: Bank interconnection with private credit is limited and well-monitored, per FSB's own May 2026 report finding banks' direct lending to private-credit funds under 0.5% of total bank assets in the five jurisdictions sampled.
stated_vs_revealed.revealed: The same FSB report simultaneously flags major data gaps, inconsistent cross-jurisdiction definitions, and limited fund/loan-level information — meaning the reassuring 0.5% figure covers only the specific, directly-measurable bank-lending channel and does not capture NAV-lending, GP-backed leverage, insurer ownership (~35% of North American insurer portfolios per IMF), or fund-level leverage structures the report itself says it cannot yet see.
stated_vs_revealed.delta: Moderate — the reassurance is real but narrower than its headline framing suggests; this is itself evidence for the Cartographer's 'least-observed' framing, sourced directly from the regulator that is trying and largely failing to observe it.

tripwires.if: a top-5 private-credit manager faces a wave of LP redemption requests it cannot meet within stated windows
tripwires.then: expect gates/suspensions, forced asset sales at a discount to book marks, and a rapid, public repricing event that had been invisible until the gate — the March 2026 episode is the template

tripwires.if: US private-credit default rates continue rising past the April 2026 record of 6.0%
tripwires.then: insurer capital positions tied to private-credit and BDC holdings come under NAIC/EIOPA scrutiny given the ~35% NA insurer portfolio share, transmitting stress into AM_ACTIVE

tripwires.if: a systemically large NAV-lending or GP-leverage exposure surfaces that the FSB's bank-exposure data (<0.5% of bank assets) did not capture
tripwires.then: treat this as confirmation that the FSB's own headline reassurance figure materially understates true bank interconnection

what_would_change_my_mind: Loan-level or fund-level regulatory data (rather than manager-reported AUM and aggregate default rates) on actual realized losses through the 2026 stress episode would let me replace the current qualitative 'meltdown' framing with a quantified loss distribution; the FSB and NAIC both say this data does not yet exist in usable form.
